short: Which labs are accredited for what
who: Calibration labs, and the people who buy calibration, who want one table saying who is accredited for which measurement and in what range.
note: BORN NOT FOR SALE. THE TABLE HOLDS NO ROWS AND THE PAGE SAYS SO IN WORDS. There is no engine lane behind this family, no store, no database and no fetched row: nothing under revenue-2026/projects belongs to it, and scripts/slice_scope_line.py REFUSES TO BUILD if a lane folder, a store file or a sample file ever appears at any of the places one would be, because the page says in words that no pass has been run and that sentence stops being true the moment one does. DATES COME FROM EVIDENCE, NEVER FROM THIS MACHINE'S CLOCK, which reads two different days depending which setting is asked. Every date on the page is read at build time out of one of two dated files: the licence read at plans/new-revenue-2026-08/wave4-working/licences/summary-registers.json (question 1, generated 2026-08-25T04:46:00Z, fetches between 04:44:20Z and 04:45:30Z that same day) and the written plan at plans/new-revenue-2026-08/PART-7-WHAT-IS-LEFT-AND-NEXT-2026-08-25.md, whose date is read off its own 'Written' line and cross-checked against the date in its file name -- a disagreement between those two refuses the build. THE REGISTER IS A2LA AND THE PAGE DOES NOT NAME IT. Their crawl rules allow crawling with a ten-second gap and the directory host publishes no crawl rules at all, but this estate's own bar for naming a source on a public page is a permission note under revenue-2026/permissions whose verdict is 'allowed', and there is no note for that host -- counted at build time, 0 of 21. Writing one is the operator's decision and no page may self-grant it, so the page says 'the register' throughout and says why. The builder derives the forbidden words from the addresses in the licence file itself and REFUSES TO BUILD if any of them reaches the rendered page, and it refuses in the other direction too: the day a permission note for that host appears, the page's stated reason for not naming it has stopped being true and the build stops until the page is rewritten. THE LICENCE VERDICTS ARE REPEATED WORD FOR WORD AND NEVER IMPROVED. Publishing derived facts on our own free page is recorded as ALLOW_FREE_ONLY; putting those same derived facts inside a file a buyer pays for is recorded as UNKNOWN; republishing the text of their scope documents is recorded as REFUSE. The builder reads all three out of the JSON summary AND out of the markdown record and refuses to build if the two copies disagree, and it refuses to build at all unless the free-page verdict is still ALLOW_FREE_ONLY. One recorded reason names the register, so it is not reprinted on the page and the page says that is why, naming the file and section where it can be read. NOTHING HAS EVER BEEN SOLD AND NO NUMBER, DATE, PRICE, GROUP, CADENCE OR BUYER IS TYPED INTO THE PAGE. Group, cadence, cadence_long, buyer, price and short all come out of this row with NO fallback; the buyer sentence is cross-checked word for word against the plan's own 'Who pays, and when' cell and a disagreement refuses the build; the kill bar, the ending event and the description of what the table would hold are read out of the plan's table row for this build at build time. The builder renders the finished page and scans the bytes: a dollar amount anywhere on it refuses the build, which is what stops the amounts in the plan's own price cell -- a cell this row deliberately does not repeat, because a remembered price and a live one look the same to anyone grepping this file -- from ever leaking onto a page whose price is 'Not for sale yet'. THE WRITTEN KILL BAR IS ON THE PAGE AND ITS CLOCK HAS NOT STARTED. The plan's bar is 'fewer than 12 rows loaded in 60 days'; that clock starts only when a priced page is live, this page carries no amount, and the page says so rather than implying a countdown is running. THE PASS ARITHMETIC IS CHECKED, NOT COPIED: the plan says 4,300 certificates at ten seconds each is a twelve-hour pass, and the builder checks that ten seconds is the crawl gap the register's own robots file asks for and that the certificates multiplied by that gap really do round to the stated hours -- either contradiction refuses the build. SAMPLE STATUS IS 'on-page' AND THE CHOICE IS DELIBERATE. The alternatives, 'fail' and 'unknown', both make the page say the sample is not ready, and that sentence tells a stranger a file is on its way. None is: there is no store, no pass and no licence answer for a paid file, so promising a sample would be the page making a promise nobody can keep. 'on-page' says the whole of what we hold is printed on this page, and with nothing held that is a sentence a stranger can check and find true -- there is no file to ask for, no store to open and nothing withheld. The builder proves it on every build rather than asserting it, by refusing to build if a store or a sample file appears, and by checking its own rendered bytes carry the on-page sentence. THERE IS NO FORM, NO UPLOAD, NO ACCOUNT AND NO SELF-SERVE ANYTHING -- this estate's platform is not ours to add one to. The only way in is an email thread with a person. STILL TO WIRE, FOR WHOEVER MERGES THIS: there is deliberately no scripts/family_status.py row, because there is no store to read a freshness date out of; 'on-page' is the one status scripts/check_built.py skips with its own printed reason for exactly that case, so the merged page passes the built-tree gate with 0 freshness tags, which is the honest number.
